issues.failure_explanation: Condition (iii) controls only the upper marginal generator of Z, not its coupling with Y or X². For example, take X=0 and an upper expectation over two Y=0 symmetric models with stable-tail coefficients a<b, and a Y=1 symmetric model with tail coefficient c(r)=a+(b-a)(1+sin(log log r))/2 for large r. Uniform O(r^(-α)) tails give the required scaled-sum bound. Slow variation makes the marginal generator asymptotically c(s^(-1/α))L, which is hidden between the two endpoint generators, so (iii) holds. The mixed generator is instead max{aLφ,bLφ,p+c(s^(-1/α))Lφ}, which can oscillate. For sufficiently large p, the bounded Lipschitz payoff p·clip(y,0,1)+cos(z) selects the Y=1 model at every step; its normalized-sum expectations have different subsequential limits. Thus the stated joint convergence need not hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require convergence of the full mixed one-step generator, as imposed later in condition (vi), and reformulate the recalled limit theorem under that stronger hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The recalled theorem's full-sequence joint convergence under only (i)–(iii) is false. The later rate results impose the additional mixed consistency condition (vi), so this particular missing hypothesis does not by itself invalidate their strengthened regime.
issues.title: Marginal jump consistency does not ensure a joint robust limit
